title: Recipes from the River: Braised Green Beans with Pickled Mustard Greens
contentHtml:
This side dish deserves a spot at your table: Whether that's at a remote campsite or your family's Thanksgiving feast.

The original idea for this dish naturally grew into one where green beans are braised with mustard greens—the ingredient that gives Sichuan-style dry-fried green beans their distinctively deep flavor. The final result is zesty, bright, and everything right.

We served this side on night two of the Moab Music Festival alongside Stir-Fried Shrimp and Grits and a Cucumber and Red Onion Salad.

This is our final Recipe from the River, and it serves as the perfect bridge between our Cooking on the River series and our Warm and Koji Thanksgiving content! Stay tuned—it all starts this weekend.

Every recipe I publish here is personally tested, tasted, and approved.

Serves: 6

Ingredients

  • Neutral oil

  • 1 medium yellow onion, thinly sliced

  • 3 garlic cloves, thinly sliced to ½ cup chopped pickled or preserved mustard greens

  • 2 pounds green beans, trimmed and cut into bite-sized pieces

  • About 1 ½ cups stock or water, plus more as needed

  • 2 tablespoons unsalted butter

  • ¼ cup cider vinegar

  • 2 tablespoons Chinese black or Chinkiang vinegar

  • Sugar

  • Kosher salt

  • Freshly ground black pepper

Method

  1. Cook the veg. Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large saucepan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add the onion and cook, stirring, until softened, about 3 minutes. Add the garlic and preserved mustard greens and stir to combine. Add the chopped green beans, stock, butter, vinegars, and a large pinch of sugar.

  2. Reduce and serve. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer. Cover and cook, stirring every 15 minutes or so, until the green beans are unreasonably tender and the sauce has reduced. This will take about an hour. Adjust seasoning with salt, pepper, vinegar, or sugar, and serve.
